paper_title: VisuoThink Empowering LVLM Reasoning with Multimodal Tree Search
caption: (LEFT) The trend of Pass@1 rate on Visual Navigation as the number of reasoning steps increases. (right) The relationship between the Accuracy@1 on geometry problems (Geomverse) and tree width for rollout search. We observe that LVLMs significantly benefit from longer reasoning chains, although the effect plateaus rapidly beyond a certain threshold of reasoning steps. The relationship between performance and tree width exhibits a more complex pattern, demonstrating an inverted U-shaped trend with both GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates the relationship between Accuracy@1 on geometry problems and tree width for rollout search, comparing the performance of two models, GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The x-axis represents the number of child nodes (tree width), with a linear scale, ranging from 1 to 7, and tick labels at intervals of 2. The y-axis represents Accuracy@1 in percentage, with a linear scale, ranging from 15 to 35, and tick labels at intervals of 5. The plot shows two lines: the dark blue line representing GPT-4o, with a solid line style and circle markers, starts at 24.4% accuracy at a tree width of 1, increases to 34.4% at a tree width of 5, and then decreases to 31.1% at a tree width of 7; the light blue line representing Claude-3.5-Sonnet, with a solid line style and cross markers, starts at 26.7% accuracy at a tree width of 1, decreases to 20.0% at a tree width of 7, with a notable value of 27.8% at a tree width of 3 and 24.4% at a tree width of 5.
